newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- US debt vols stay bid despite bond bounce.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- US debt vols stay bid despite bond bounce.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed income options were well bid in choppy late trade as the underlying market remained shaky despite a mid-afternoon bounce on a friendly Beige Book report, dealers said.

"It's come off a little bit, but it's been relatively steady," said a brokerage T-bond trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT), adding that volatilities had risen earlier when bond prices were at their lows.
He noted that the afternoon rally lacked follow-through buying and that caution ahead of Thursday's retail sales and Friday's producer prices data underpinned volatilities.
The Federal Reserve said in its latest Beige Book that price pressures were temperate and wage gains were modest despite a tight job markets throughout the country.

June T-bond futures, which had been grinding lower for most of the day to a lot of 109-17/32 bounced back toward Tuesday's close of 110-00 on the news. But the contract soon lost steam and glided back down toward the lows.
Implied volatilities for CBOT April and June T-bond futures options were a touch above Tuesday's closing levels at 9.2 and 9.5 percent respectively just before the close.

While the Federal Open Market Committee was to look into the latest Beige Book findings when they discuss monetary policy at their March 25 meeting, traders said interest rate markets remained nervous about a credit tightening.
"I think the market is a long way from reversing to higher prices, at least at the short end," said a Eurodollar trader for a brokerage firm at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME).

"The problem is, people don't want to short the market too much because there's already so much tightening built in," he added, referring to the relatively narrow daily ranges in Eurodollar futures recently.
Traders said there were plenty of volatility buyers on dips but that it was still too early for gamma traders to bid up volatilities in speculative pre-FOMC bets because of time-decay concerns.
Shorter-dated options are often bid up before important events because they have high gamma, which gives them quick premium acceleration, but they are also vulnerable to time decay.
Implied volatilities for CME June and September Eurodollar futures options stood little changed at 10.0 and 13.0 percent respectively.
